tests.name: boolean-logic
tests.description: The Boolean logic section: and, or, xor, implies and not(); their truth tables over true, false and empty; operands evaluated as Booleans by singleton evaluation of collections (a single Boolean, a single non-Boolean item, more than one item); and the worked examples. FHIR's FHIRPath pages (R4, R5) say nothing about these operators. Where 3.0.0's implies note (an empty left side gives the right side) disagrees with the truth table, the cases follow 2.0.0. Leaves out what the text does not settle: a single String, Integer or Decimal whose value converts explicitly to false ('false', 0, 0.0), which 2.0.0 and 3.0.0 word differently; not() on a non-Boolean item or on more than one item; and whether an operand that would signal an error still does so when the other operand alone decides the result (false and X, X and false, true or X, X or true, false implies X, X implies true, X xor {}, {} xor X), since the text allows short-circuit evaluation.

Returns `true` if both operands evaluate to `true`, `false` if either operand evaluates to `false`, and the empty collection (`{ }`) otherwise.

This means that when, in an underlying data object (i.e. they physical data on which the implementation is operating) a member is null or missing, there will simply be no corresponding node for that member in the tree, e.g. `Patient.name` will return an empty collection (not null) if there are no name elements in the instance.
